title: Cap. IX Arg. 3 Sol: Docete omnes gentes / Predicate omni creaturae — apostolic authority for the whole world; wall between Jew and Gentile down
latin: Ex illis mandatis Christi Docete omnes gentes, Predicate omni creaturae, recte colligitur, Discipulis illis auctoritatem Apostolicam, id est, non particulari alicui Ecclesiae aut nationi affixam, sed ad totum terrarum orbem spectantem, fuisse demandatam. Recte etiam infertur, Maceriam illam, quae Gentes ab Ecclesia Dei disterminavit, dirutam fuisse, et debuisse Evangelium, non uni nationi Judaeorum, sed Judaeis et Gentibus, Graecis et barbaris, sapientibus et insipientibus, praedicari, ut loquitur Paulus Rom. i.
pass_a: From those mandates of Christ, Teach all nations, Preach to every creature, it is rightly gathered that Apostolic authority was committed unto those Disciples, that is, authority not affixed unto any particular Church or nation, but looking unto the whole orb of the lands. It is also rightly inferred that that partition-wall which divided the Gentiles from the Church of God was thrown down, and that the Gospel ought to be preached not unto one nation of the Jews alone, but unto Jews and Gentiles, Greeks and barbarians, wise and unwise, as Paul speaks Rom. i.
pass_b: From Christ's charges Teach all nations and Preach to every creature it rightly follows that those disciples were given apostolic authority — not pinned to one church or nation, but aimed at the whole world. It also follows that the wall which shut Gentiles from God's church was broken down, and that the Gospel was to be preached not to Jews alone but to Jews and Gentiles, Greeks and barbarians, wise and unwise — as Paul says in Rom. 1.

lemmas.gloss: apostolic charge for the whole world, not one nation

title: Cap. IX Arg. 3 Sol: ministers must seek to bring every hearer to Christ — Augustine De correptione et gratia 15
latin: Denique et illud recte deducitur, Intentionem et operam ministrorum Evangelicorum eo spectare oportere, ac Pauli operam eo spectasse, ut eos omnes et singulos ad Christum adduceret, quibus Evangelium Christi annunciavit. Nam, ut pie et prudenter Augustinus, Nos nescientes quis pertineat ad praedestinatorum numerum, quis non pertineat, sic affici debemus charitatis affectu, ut omnes velimus salvos fieri, De corrupt. et grat. cap. 15.
pass_a: Finally that also is rightly deduced, that the intention and labor of the ministers of the Gospel ought to look thither, and that Paul's labor looked thither, that he might bring unto Christ all and singular those unto whom he announced the Gospel of Christ. For, as Augustine piously and prudently, We, not knowing who pertains unto the number of the predestined, who does not pertain, ought so to be affected with the affection of charity, that we will all to be saved, De corrupt. et grat. cap. 15.
pass_b: Finally it also follows that Gospel ministers' aim and labor — as Paul's did — ought to be to bring to Christ every one to whom they announce Christ's Gospel. As Augustine says with piety and prudence: not knowing who belongs to the number of the predestined and who does not, we ought to be so moved by charity that we will all to be saved (De corrept. et grat. 15).

lemmas.gloss: ministers aim to bring every hearer to Christ
charity wills all saved though elect number unknown

title: Cap. IX Arg. 3 Sol: deny adversaries' corollary — reprobation of those to whom Christ ordered preaching is not only from foresight of demerits
latin: Sed, hisce omnibus admissis, negamus illud consectarium quod ex talibus testimoniis exprimere conantur adversarii, nempe, Illos non nisi ex praevisione demeritorum suorum fuisse reprobatos, quibus hunc in modum Christus jussit Evangelium praedicari. Nam reprobare est ex decreto suae voluntatis permittere aliquos a fine beatitudinis deficere, non destinando ac praeparando illis specialem illam gratiam, qua reapse ad fidem et vitam aeternam perducerentur: sicuti eligere est ad beatitudinem consequendam aliquos infallibiliter et infrustrabiliter ordinare, destinando, praeparando, ac donando illis specialem illam gratiam, qua Deus ab aeterno statuit et intellexit eos fore emolliendos, convertendos et de facto salvandos.
pass_a: But, these things all being admitted, we deny that corollary which from such testimonies the adversaries endeavor to express, namely, That those unto whom Christ so commanded the Gospel to be preached were not reprobated except from foresight of their demerits. For to reprobate is, from the decree of his will, to permit some to fall short of the end of beatitude, by not destining and preparing unto them that special grace by which they would in fact be led unto faith and eternal life: as to elect is to ordain some unto the obtaining of beatitude infallibly and unfrustrably, by destining, preparing, and giving unto them that special grace by which God from eternity decreed and understood that they would be softened, converted, and in fact saved.
pass_b: All that granted, we still deny the adversaries' corollary from these texts: that those to whom Christ ordered the Gospel preached were reprobated only from foresight of their demerits. To reprobate is, by decree of will, to permit some to fall short of beatitude's end — not destining or preparing for them that special grace which would in fact lead them to faith and eternal life. To elect is to ordain some to obtain beatitude infallibly and without frustration — destining, preparing, and giving them that special grace by which God from eternity decreed and knew they would be softened, converted, and in fact saved.

lemmas.gloss: deny reprobation only from foresight demerits
reprobation = withhold special grace; election = give it infallibly

title: Cap. IX Arg. 3 Sol: evangelizing mandate does not clash with reprobating will — passover antecedes final hardness, not from foresight of it
latin: Jam vero jubemur Evangelium multis praedicare, quos Deus in hac infallibili ordinatione ad gratiam et gloriam, ex mero suo beneplacito, voluit praeterire. Mandatum igitur Evangelizandi non pugnat cum voluntate reprobandi. Addo etiam, Praeterire illos voluit, quoad praeparationem specialis hujus gratiae et de facto salutiferae, voluntate duritiam illorum finalem antecedente, et non ex praevisione finalis hujus duritiae et infidelitatis emanante. Nam (ut saepe dictum est) finalis impoenitentia et infidelitas hujus aut illius singularis personae non praevidetur aut praeconsideratur a Deo tanquam absolute et certo futura, nisi decreto reprobationis quoad eandem personam stabilito, quo Deus statuit, nolle talis personae eousque misereri ut efficaciter eam emolliat et convertat; quo etiam statuit, velle permittere ut suo vitio quamlibet gratiam oblatam repellat, et obduratus corde ad finem usque vitae suae permaneat.
pass_a: Now truly we are commanded to preach the Gospel unto many whom God in this infallible ordination unto grace and glory, from his mere good pleasure, willed to pass by. The mandate of evangelizing therefore does not fight with the will of reprobating. I add also, He willed to pass them by, as to the preparation of this special and in-fact saving grace, by a will preceding their final hardness, and not emanating from foresight of this final hardness and unbelief. For (as has often been said) the final impenitence and unbelief of this or that singular person is not foreseen or preconsidered by God as absolutely and certainly future, except the decree of reprobation concerning the same person being established, by which God decreed not to pity such a person so far as to soften and convert him efficaciously; by which also he decreed to will to permit that by his own vice he repel any grace offered, and remain hardened in heart unto the end of his life.
pass_b: We are commanded to preach the Gospel to many whom God, in that infallible ordination to grace and glory, from mere good pleasure willed to pass by. So the evangelizing mandate does not clash with the reprobating will. I add: he willed to pass them by as to preparing this special, actually saving grace — by a will that precedes their final hardness, not one that flows from foresight of that final hardness and unbelief. For (as often said) a particular person's final impenitence and unbelief is not foreseen by God as absolutely certain until the reprobation decree for that person stands — whereby God decreed not to pity them so far as to soften and convert them efficaciously, and also decreed to permit them by their own vice to repel any offered grace and stay hard-hearted to life's end.

lemmas.gloss: passover precedes final hardness; not from foresight of it

title: Cap. IX Arg. 3 Sol: Matt. 11:25; 13:11; Rom. 9:18 — antecedent good pleasure where the word was preached; efficacious grace prepared for some only
latin: Huc spectant illa Servatoris verba, Matth. xi. 25. Gloriam tibi tribuo Pater Domine caeli ac terrae, quod absconderis haec a sapientibus et intelligentibus, et ea detexeris infantibus. Etiam, Pater, quia ita placuit tibi. Et illa, Matth. xiii. 11. Vobis datum est nosse mysteria regni caelorum; illis non est datum. Denique et illud Apostoli, saepe inculcatum ac inculcandum omnibus specialis gratiae adversariis, Cujus vult miseretur, quem autem vult indurat, Rom. ix. 18. Omnia haec loca illos respiciunt quibus Dei verbum fuit praedicatum; et tamen in hisce omnibus innuatur antecedaneum Dei beneplacitum, secundum quod efficax gratia quibusdam praeparata fuit, aliis non fuit praeparata.
pass_a: Hither look those words of the Savior, Matt. xi. 25. I ascribe glory unto thee, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that thou hast hidden these things from the wise and intelligent, and hast uncovered them unto babes. Even so, Father, because it so pleased thee. And those, Matt. xiii. 11. Unto you it is given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven; unto them it is not given. Finally also that of the Apostle, often inculcated and to be inculcated unto all adversaries of special grace, Of whom he will he has mercy, and whom he will he hardens, Rom. ix. 18. All these places regard those unto whom the word of God was preached; and yet in all these is hinted the antecedent good pleasure of God, according to which efficacious grace was prepared for some, for others was not prepared.
pass_b: Here belong the Savior's words, Matt. 11:25: I give you glory, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that you have hidden these things from the wise and understanding and uncovered them to infants. Yes, Father, for so it pleased you. And Matt. 13:11: To you it is given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven; to them it is not given. And that saying of the Apostle, often pressed against every foe of special grace: He has mercy on whom he will, and whom he will he hardens (Rom. 9:18). All these texts concern those to whom God's word was preached — and yet in all of them God's antecedent good pleasure is hinted: efficacious grace prepared for some, not prepared for others.

lemmas.gloss: efficacious grace prepared for some only

title: Cap. IX Arg. 3 Sol: physician analogy — command to preach to all does not prove God decreed to free all efficaciously
latin: Ut verbo absolvam, sicuti ex eo quod Deus vult omnes medicos pro sua virili ea agere, parare et offerre cuilibet aegroto quem curandum suscipiunt, quae ad vitam ejus producendam conducunt, non recte infertur Deum nolle permittere ut vi morbi ullus extinguatur, nisi exinde quod eundem praeviderit ut medicinae oblatae praefractum contemptorem: sic ex eo quod jubet Deus ministros Evangelicos verbum (quod est animorum medicina) omnibus praedicare, et omni ope eniti, ut omnes et singuli a morte liberentur, non sequitur, ipsum Deum decrevisse omnes a morte efficaciter liberare, aut non decrevisse permittere quosdam sua duricordia in perditionem ruere, quos nisi reprobasset, et potuisset et voluisset speciali sua misericordia emollire. Frustra igitur ex voluntate Dei mandante, quae actiones humanas debet gubernare, de voluntate Dei praedestinante aut reprobante judicatur, quae effectum aliquem producendum infallibili actione Divina, aut ea negata non producendum, determinat.
pass_a: To finish in a word: as from this, that God wills all physicians according to their strength so to act, to prepare and offer unto any sick man whom they take to cure those things which conduce unto prolonging his life, it is not rightly inferred that God wills not to permit any to be extinguished by force of disease, except from this, that he foresaw the same as a stubborn contemner of the medicine offered: so from this, that God commands the ministers of the Gospel to preach the word (which is the medicine of souls) unto all, and with all might to strive that all and singular be freed from death, it does not follow that God himself decreed to free all from death efficaciously, or did not decree to permit some by their hard-heartedness to rush into perdition, whom unless he had reprobated, he both could and would have softened by his special mercy. In vain therefore from the mandating will of God, which ought to govern human actions, is judgment made concerning the predestinating or reprobating will of God, which determines some effect to be produced by infallible Divine action, or, that denied, not to be produced.
pass_b: In a word: from God's will that every physician do his utmost — prepare and offer each patient he takes on whatever helps prolong life — you may not infer that God will let none die of disease unless he foresaw him a stubborn scorner of the offered medicine. So from God's command that Gospel ministers preach the word (the medicine of souls) to all, and strain every nerve that every one be freed from death, it does not follow that God himself decreed to free all from death efficaciously — or that he did not decree to permit some, by their hard hearts, to rush into perdition whom, had he not reprobated them, he both could and would have softened by special mercy. Vain, then, to judge the predestinating or reprobating will — which determines an effect by infallible divine action, or withholds it — from the mandating will that ought to govern human actions.
